newsitem.title: USA: Reebok CEO raises stake after auction.
newsitem.headline: Reebok CEO raises stake after auction.

text.p: Reebok International Ltd said Chief Executive Paul Fireman holds about 22 percent of the outstanding shares of the footwear company following completion of the "Dutch auction" announced earlier.
Fireman and his wife, Phyllis, who elected not to tender their shares in the auction, raised their stake from 16.9 percent before the auction, spokeswoman Kete Burnham said.
Holders of 17.02 million shares sold their stock at $36 each for a total cost of $612.7 million to Reebok, Burnham said.
When the Dutch auction was announced in late July, Reebok offered to buy back up to 24 million of the shares at a price between $30 and $36 each.
"I think that management is happy with getting 17 million shares," Burnham said.
Analysts said they were surprised at the large number of shareholders who tendered, since Reebok was offering little premium to the market price of the shares.

"I'm surprised it's even 17 million. I thought it was not going to be a big tender at all," the analyst said. "I don't see the stock doing anything near-term in spite of this tender. This is the top management trying to instill some confidence in the stock with the market."
Peter Russ, a securities analyst with Shelby, Cullom & Davis Co, said most shareholders he talked to said they planned to hold their shares.
"I was surprised by how much was tendered. I was predicting 12 to 15 million shares. It was clear it was going to be done at $36," said Russ, whose clients hold about 10 million shares.
